summary: The address the boot line gives the machine, found in what the machine sends

cases.behavior: the machine takes the address rach2.ip gives it, 10.0.2.77, and pingtest passes; the capture of the rtl8139 has a packet sent from that address and an ARP request sent as it

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine when the scenario did not power it off

steps.does: boot the test image with rach2.ip=10.0.2.77/24 and rach2.gateway=10.0.2.2 to the debug shell
run pingtest at the debug shell and take its report from the console
power the machine off at the debug shell and wait for its end, which makes the capture whole
run pcapcheck bcast on the capture of the card for a packet sent from 10.0.2.77 and an ARP request sent as 10.0.2.77

assertions.checks: three pings to the gateway each get a reply
a ping to an address nobody answers fails
the child writes its byte just before its ping, and /proc shows it asleep in the call
while the child is in its call, the parent's ping of the loopback address answers EBUSY
the parent's clock readings while the child waits span some time, so the wait sleeps
the child reports the length of its call through the pipe
the child is reaped and exited normally
the child's call lasted at least 3990 ms, the kernel's four hundred ticks
after the reap the parent's loopback ping returns a round-trip time of 0 or more
a data ping of 1473 bytes, and on x86-64 one of a size past 32 bits, is refused with EMSGSIZE
the machine powers off at the debug shell's command after pingtest, so that the capture is whole
pcapcheck bcast finds in the capture of the card a packet sent from 10.0.2.77 and an ARP request sent as 10.0.2.77

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the address is given on the boot line, and pcapcheck reads QEMU's capture of the card's frames; tests/native/probes.cases runs pingtest's rows natively
